title: Office — the last loose ends before the definition of done

steps.path: A conversation → Session files → Garden plan.docx → Edit
steps.headline: The editor's scroll bars and the gap above the page are gone; the document fills the panel edge to edge.
steps.changed: Your round-2 note: the editor's own chunky scroll bars and the band above the first page now sit just outside the panel, where they are cropped away.
steps.notice: The page starts right under the slim toolbar, and the text is a little larger again. Mouse wheel, trackpad and touch still scroll.
steps.risk: There is no scroll bar to drag in this small editor; the full Office page keeps the editor's own.

steps.headline: Should LibreOffice files be in the first version, or added later?
steps.today: You picked Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV, old Office files and LibreOffice files, with a note that LibreOffice files can wait if they are a lot of work.
steps.problem: The same translator already opens and saves them, so the work is testing, not building — but every format is more to check before the first version.

options.label: In the first version
pros: LibreOffice users' files open from day one.
Little extra work: the translator already handles them.
cons: A few more days of testing before the first version.

options.label: Later, on the roadmap
pros: The first version arrives slightly sooner.
cons: A LibreOffice file shows only its name until then.

steps.path: Editing a CSV table in Office
steps.headline: Before saving a CSV, Office warns if anything you added — colours, a second sheet, formulas — cannot be kept in that format.
steps.changed: Your note on file types: "we should handle csv but warn if something would cause an issue". The warning offers to save a spreadsheet copy instead.
steps.notice: A CSV with only plain values saves silently, as it does today.

steps.path: Chatting while a document is open
steps.headline: This version of Office adds nothing to the assistant: it neither sees nor edits open documents. It is your own editing tool.
steps.changed: Your notes on the two assistant questions said not to change assistant behaviour for now, so the "straight in, undoable" pick is set aside for a later version.
steps.notice: The assistant can still read and write the files themselves, as it does today.

steps.path: The Office editor under your current theme
steps.headline: Theme matching includes your theme's roundness: the editor's buttons, menus, fields and dialogs use your theme's corner sizes.
steps.changed: Your note on theming asked for the roundness settings too. The editor has corner settings for all of those; Halftone Dimension's large corners already showed in round 1.
steps.notice: A handful of the editor's own shapes with fixed corners stay square; those are fixed by hand during the build.

steps.headline: Office ships inside the YouCoded installer as a separate program, which its licence allows, with its notices and a link to its code.
steps.changed: Your note on the download question asked if bundling is allowed. The licence explicitly permits shipping separate programs together, as long as its notices and code link are included.
steps.notice: Every YouCoded download grows by about 80 MB; Office can still update between app releases.
steps.risk: The lawyer check we planned before launch still applies to the separate-program arrangement as a whole.
